newsitem.title: USA: Fruehauf files for Chapter 11 protection.
newsitem.headline: Fruehauf files for Chapter 11 protection.

text.p: Fruehauf Trailer Corp said Monday it has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, seeking to restore liquidity by permitting it to reorganize its finances.
The filings do not include the company's Mexican operating subsidiary, Fruehauf de Mexico SA de CV, it said.
The company said it has $55 million in debtor-in-possession financing from an affiliate of Cerberus Partners LP.
Fruehauf also announced that three board members are resigning, following the previous resignations of four other board members.
The line of credit, which is subject to approval by the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware, will be used to repay debts under its revolving credit and to meet immediate and future inventory needs.
It also will be used to satisfy existing customer and employee obligations, to pay new vendor invoices promptly and to operate its business, Fruehauf said.
Fruehauf said it will continue to manufacture, service and distribute trailers and parts.

The company said that Raymond Dempsey, Anthony Miller and Richard Nevins have resigned from the board of directors. Their resignations are effective with the consummation of the debtor-in-possession facility.
Four other board members -- Thomas Roller, Timothy Wiggins, William Panny and Marvin Rosenberg -- resigned previously from the board.
The company will have a four-member board consisting of Chriss Street, Worth Frederick and two additional directors to be appointed to fill the vacancies.
The bankruptcy filing comes a little over a month after the company named its new president, Derek Nagle, who previously was its executive vice president of North American operations.
His predecessor, Thomas Roller, resigned to become president and chief executive of Wolverine Tube Inc.
Fruehauf manufactures truck trailers, and produces, markets and services dry-freight van, refrigerated van and tank trailers.
Fruehauf Corp and nine subsidiaries filed 10 petitions in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Del. The company listed assets of $182.4 million and liabilities of $251.8 million.
Judge Peter Walsh approved orders allowing the company to continue normal business operations.
